name: NexusFlow Demand Planning
description: A demand-planning workspace that combines sell-out, dealer, and plant data so manufacturers can forecast SKU-level demand and reduce stockouts without adding planner headcount.
icp: Branded manufacturers with 500+ SKUs, multi-depot networks, and a mix of modern trade plus traditional dealers.
value_props: SKU-depot forecasts that planners can explain to finance
Faster consensus planning between sales, supply, and plants
use_cases: Promotional lift planning for festive seasons
differentiators: Built for India dealer and distributor data, not only modern-trade POS
Works with existing SAP or Oracle planning extracts
Planners keep control; the model does not silently overwrite the plan
objections: We already have SAP IBP or a homegrown Excel model
Master data across depots is too messy
IT does not want another planning system
pricing_model: Annual subscription by number of active SKUs and depots. Implementation is scoped separately.
proof_points: A South India coatings manufacturer cut depot emergency transfers by 18% in two quarters.
A durables brand reduced festive-season stockouts on top 200 SKUs without raising safety stock.

name: NexusFlow PlantConnect
description: A plant-visibility layer that pulls machine, batch, and downtime signals into one operations view so plant and central teams can see bottlenecks the same way.
icp: Process and discrete manufacturers running multiple plants, with a live Industry 4.0 or reliability program.
value_props: One downtime and throughput picture across plants
Faster root-cause reviews without waiting for a monthly MIS
Connects to common historians and PLC gateways
differentiators: Does not require ripping out the existing MES
Role-based views for plant heads and central ops
India-first implementation partners and on-site support
objections: We are already buying a historian or APM suite
Plant teams will not adopt another dashboard
pricing_model: Annual subscription per connected production line, plus a one-time plant onboarding fee.
proof_points: A multi-plant metals customer cut unplanned downtime review time from days to the same shift.
A coatings plant used line-level visibility to justify a single bottleneck capex instead of a full line upgrade.

name: NexusFlow TradePulse
description: Dealer and distributor analytics that show which outlets, regions, and influencers are actually moving product, so channel teams stop managing the network from last month's Excel.
icp: Branded companies with 1,000+ dealers or distributors and a growing influencer or painter/contractor program.
value_props: Live dealer health instead of month-end claims
Better targeting of painter, electrician, or contractor programs
Early warning when a high-potential depot starts slipping
differentiators: Handles cash-and-carry and informal dealer data, not only DMS-perfect accounts
Connects claims, secondary sales, and program spend
objections: Our DMS is already supposed to do this
Dealers will not share secondary data
Regional teams will see this as surveillance
pricing_model: Annual subscription by active dealers plus optional influencer-program module.
proof_points: An electricals brand found 14% of program spend sitting on inactive influencers.
A coatings company used depot-level secondary sales to reopen a stalled East India expansion case.
